claims.feature: other: Le Guin's judgment of Wolfe's fiction
claims.claim: Le Guin's blurb for The Urth of the New Sun says the groundnote of the whole book is human pain.
claims.source: Ursula K. Le Guin, publisher's praise for Gene Wolfe, The Urth of the New Sun (Tor/Macmillan)
claims.quote: The groundnote of it all is human pain
claims.page: Praise for The Urth of the New Sun

claims.feature: other: Le Guin's judgment of Wolfe's fiction
claims.claim: Le Guin's blurb argues that it is the human pain in Wolfe's book that gives the fantasy the weight of vision.
claims.source: Ursula K. Le Guin, publisher's praise for Gene Wolfe, The Urth of the New Sun (Tor/Macmillan)
claims.quote: so that this fantasy has the weight of vision
claims.page: Praise for The Urth of the New Sun

claims.claim: Le Guin describes the motion of Wolfe's book in The Urth of the New Sun with three verbs of increasing release, soaring, falling free and running.
claims.source: Ursula K. Le Guin, publisher's praise for Gene Wolfe, The Urth of the New Sun (Tor/Macmillan)
claims.quote: Gene Wolfe's new book soars, falls free, runs like
claims.page: Praise for The Urth of the New Sun

claims.feature: other: provenance of the Melville line
claims.claim: The publisher's praise block for The Urth of the New Sun prints Le Guin's three sentences without the sentence "Wolfe is our Melville".
claims.source: Macmillan, Praise for The Urth of the New Sun (captured 2023-05-27)
claims.page: Praise for The Urth of the New Sun

claims.feature: other: provenance of the Melville line
claims.claim: The four words "Wolfe is our Melville" are printed as Le Guin's on the jacket copy of at least five separate Wolfe books without naming any venue or date.
claims.source: Open Library search-inside over Internet Archive book scans (Soldier of Sidon, Innocents Aboard, Strange Travelers, Pirate Freedom, Soldier of Arete)

claims.feature: other: reception of the Melville line
claims.claim: John Clute calls Le Guin's Melville line a frequently requoted encomium and gives no source for it.
claims.source: John Clute, "Wolfe, Gene", The Encyclopedia of Science Fiction (sf-encyclopedia.com)

claims.feature: other: reception of the Melville line
claims.claim: Clute glosses Le Guin's Melville comparison as claiming a shared omnivorousness and grasp between Wolfe and Melville.
claims.source: John Clute, "Wolfe, Gene", The Encyclopedia of Science Fiction
claims.quote: share a vast omnivorousness and grasp

claims.feature: other: reception of the Melville line
claims.claim: The New Yorker reports the Melville line as something Le Guin said once, without naming where.
claims.source: Peter Bebergal, "Sci-Fi's Difficult Genius", The New Yorker, 2015

claims.feature: other: reception of the Melville line
claims.claim: Wikipedia's Gene Wolfe article presents the Melville line as jacket copy rather than as a sourced statement.
claims.source: Wikipedia relaying Wolfe jacket copy, article "Gene Wolfe", Reception section
claims.quote: frequently quoted on the jackets of Wolfe's books

claims.feature: other: Le Guin's standing among Wolfe's readers
claims.claim: Jeet Heer names Le Guin, with John Clute, as one of Wolfe's strongest fans.
claims.source: Jeet Heer, "Gene Wolfe Was the Proust of Science Fiction", The New Republic, April 2019
claims.quote: his strongest fans (fellow writer Ursula K. Le Guin

claims.feature: other: the thinness of the record
claims.claim: From Elfland to Poughkeepsie, Le Guin's central essay on fantasy style, does not name Gene Wolfe anywhere in its text.
claims.source: Ursula K. Le Guin, "From Elfland to Poughkeepsie" (1973), PDF at digginganddeepening.com

claims.feature: other: the thinness of the record
claims.claim: The table of contents of Words Are My Matter, Le Guin's collected 2000 to 2016 essays, book introductions and reviews, lists no piece on Gene Wolfe.
claims.source: The Ursula K. Le Guin Foundation, official site, page for Words Are My Matter

claims.feature: other: the thinness of the record
claims.claim: The table of contents of Dancing at the Edge of the World, including its reviews section, lists no piece on Gene Wolfe.
claims.source: The Ursula K. Le Guin Foundation, official site, page for Dancing at the Edge of the World

claims.feature: other: the thinness of the record
claims.claim: The table of contents of The Wave in the Mind lists appreciations of Cordwainer Smith and Borges but no piece on Gene Wolfe.
claims.source: The Ursula K. Le Guin Foundation, official site, page for The Wave in the Mind

claims.claim: Part of the correspondence series in the Ursula K. Le Guin papers is closed to researchers until 2069 at the donor's request.
claims.source: Archives West, finding aid for the Ursula K. Le Guin papers, University of Oregon Coll 270
claims.quote: closed until 2069 by request of the donor

verdicts.trueWording: The groundnote of it all is human pain
verdicts.note: Macmillan Urth of the New Sun page, blurb block (headed 'In The News', not 'Praise'), attributed to Ursula K. Le Guin. Quotation exact; every limb of the claim on the page. Wayback raw capture 20230527084143id_ fetched with a browser UA, 200.

verdicts.trueWording: so that this fantasy has the weight of vision
verdicts.note: Same Le Guin blurb, same block: the clause follows 'The groundnote of it all is human pain,' so the causal limb (pain gives the fantasy its weight of vision) is on the page.

verdicts.unsupportedLimb: 'three verbs of increasing release' - the page ranks nothing; the escalation is the claimant's gloss
verdicts.trueWording: Gene Wolfe's new book soars, falls free, runs like the river
verdicts.note: The three verbs (soars / falls free / runs) are on the page word for word in the Le Guin blurb; the page makes no claim about their being ordered by increasing release.

verdicts.unsupportedLimb: 'three sentences' - the Le Guin blurb printed there is two sentences
verdicts.trueWording: Two sentences under 'In The News'; 'Melville' absent from page
verdicts.note: CONFIRMED on the absence limb: grep of the whole captured page returns 0 occurrences of 'Melville'. The blurb block is headed 'In The News' and Le Guin's contribution runs to two sentences, not three. Related datum from index 715's page: an Open Library search-inside snippet for the printed Urth of the New Sun shows '...the weight of vision. Wolfe is our Melville.' - i.e. the book's own praise page does carry the sentence the Macmillan page omits.

verdicts.unsupportedLimb: 'jacket copy' - snippets do not show whether the line sits on the jacket or on an interior praise page
verdicts.trueWording: Six Wolfe books' snippets credit 'Wolfe is our Melville' to Le Guin
verdicts.note: Open Library search-inside fetched raw (not a summarizer): 'About 8 results'. All five books named in the source field appear - Soldier of Sidon, Innocents Aboard, Strange Travelers, Pirate Freedom, Soldier of Arete - plus The Urth of the New Sun and the reference work Something About the Author v.165. Every snippet attributes the line to Ursula K. Le Guin with no venue or date inside the snippet window; the window is truncated, so absence of a venue is shown only for the visible span, and placement (jacket vs front matter) is not shown at all.

sf-encyclopedia.com/entry/wolfe_gene, entry body, signed [JC] (John Clute): 'Ursula K Le Guin's frequently requoted encomium - "Wolfe is our Melville" - ...'. No venue, date or citation for the line anywhere in the entry or its links block, so the second limb holds too.

verdicts.trueWording: share a vast omnivorousness and grasp
verdicts.note: Same sentence: Clute writes the line 'may be fairly understood to suggest that both authors share a vast omnivorousness and grasp', exemplified by The Book of the New Sun and Moby-Dick. Clute's hedge ('may be fairly understood') is softer than the claim's 'glosses ... as claiming', but the gloss is his and the quotation is exact.

verdicts.trueWording: Ursula K. Le Guin once called Wolfe “our Melville.”
verdicts.note: newyorker.com 'Sci-Fi's Difficult Genius', by Peter Bebergal, April 24, 2015, article body; live URL fetched raw with a browser UA, 200. The quoted string 'Le Guin once called Wolfe' appears word for word, and no venue or date for the remark is given anywhere in the piece.

verdicts.unsupportedLimb: 'rather than as a sourced statement' - the lead states the same line with two citations (New Yorker 2015, SFE)
verdicts.trueWording: frequently quoted on the jackets of Wolfe's books
verdicts.note: action=raw wikitext fetched. The quoted phrase is verbatim in the Reception section (line 69, uncited): 'Ursula K. Le Guin is frequently quoted on the jackets of Wolfe's books as having said "Wolfe is our Melville."' But the article lead (line 30) says 'Ursula K. Le Guin called Wolfe "our Melville"' carrying refs name=new-yorker-2015 and name=SFE, so the article does also present it as sourced.

verdicts.trueWording: many of his strongest fans (fellow writer Ursula K. Le Guin
verdicts.note: newrepublic.com, Jeet Heer, April 18, 2019, body paragraph on Wolfe's Catholicism: the parenthesis continues 'and critic John Clute) are decidedly not Catholics themselves.' Byline, outlet and date all on the page; live fetch 200.

verdicts.trueWording: 'Wolfe' occurs zero times in the eight-page essay PDF
verdicts.note: PDF binary fetched (346,717 bytes, 8 pages) and text-extracted with pdftotext: 5,118 words, opening 'Elfland is what Lord Dunsany called the place', closing 'nothing, after all, is realer.' Case-insensitive grep for 'wolfe' and for 'melville' returns nothing. Claim carries no quotation, hence SUBSTANCE not VERBATIM; 'central essay on fantasy style' is the claimant's descriptor, and the essay is indeed about style in fantasy.

verdicts.unsupportedLimb: 'collected 2000 to 2016' - the page's cover alt text reads 'Writings About Life and Books, 2006-2016'
verdicts.trueWording: Contents lists no Wolfe piece; cover alt says 2006-2016
verdicts.note: ursulakleguin.com/words-are-my-matter fetched raw. The full Table of Contents (Foreword; Talks, Essays and Occasional Pieces; Book Introductions and Notes on Writers; Book Reviews; Excerpt; Supplements) contains 0 occurrences of 'Wolfe'. The page describes the book as collecting 'talks, essays, introductions to beloved books, and book reviews' and never prints a 2000 start year.

verdicts.trueWording: Table of Contents and REVIEWS name no Gene Wolfe
verdicts.note: ursulakleguin.com/dancing-at-the-edge-of-the-world fetched raw. Full Contents plus the REVIEWS run (Lewis, Lessing x3, Gardner, Calvino x2, Peake, Scarf, Bierhorst, Linden, Gloss, See, Wood and others) contains 0 occurrences of 'Wolfe'. No quotation in the claim, hence SUBSTANCE.

ursulakleguin.com/the-wave-in-the-mind, Table of Contents, 'Readings' section: '“Thinking about Cordwainer Smith”' verbatim, and in the same section '“Things Not Actually Present: On The Book of Fantasy and J.L. Borges”'. 0 occurrences of 'Wolfe' on the page. 'Appreciations' is the claimant's descriptor for those two pieces.

verdicts.trueWording: closed until 2069 by request of the donor
verdicts.note: archiveswest.orbiscascade.org/ark:/80444/xv926878, Access Restrictions: 'The correspondence series in boxes 253 is closed until 2069 by request of the donor.' Collection is University of Oregon Coll 270, Ursula K. Le Guin papers; the restriction covers part of the series (boxes 253), matching the claim's 'part'. Same block also closes selected email until 2043.
